lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.history: The first K&R book described the language as used in the late 1970s. The subsequent standard documented later language and library details more formally.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Martin Richards designed BCPL. Thompson drew on it for B, and Ritchie developed C from B while working on Unix.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: C is general-purpose, procedural and imperative. Middle-level is an informal teaching label. A compiler accepting a program does not prove that it works or runs unchanged everywhere.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: Compare claims about a language's facilities with claims about a particular program. Testing the program and reviewing portability are still part of the work.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: General-purpose is about the kinds of tasks a language can express. Procedural is about organizing work into functions. Imperative is about executing instructions that can change state.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual
